turns.t: Good morning, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I'm afraid it's rather a small thing, these warts on my hands.
Not at all. Tell me about them.
Well, the first one appeared on my right thumb, and now there are a few more along my fingers.
Which hand has most of them?
Mainly the right, though two have crept onto the left, I'm sorry to say.
Mm-hm. And when did you first notice the one on your thumb?
About four months ago, I'd say. I thought it was a bit of hard skin at first.
And how have they changed since then?
They've multiplied. There were two, and now I count seven or eight.
What does it feel like, having them?
Rough, mostly. They catch on the wool of my gloves, and that's a nuisance.
Do they itch or hurt at all?
No, neither of those. They just look dreadful. My granddaughter won't hold my hand!
Ah, now. What's been bothering you most about them?
Honestly, the look of them, and I'd hate to pass them on to anyone.
That's a very reasonable thing to think about. Do you have any idea where they came from?
A neighbour's lad had them last summer, but I wouldn't like to blame him.
Nobody can ever say for sure where they come from, so don't be blaming yourself either.
I see. Well, I'd just like to know whether there's anything to be done.
There are a few options, and we'll go through them. First, would you hold your hands out under the light for me?
Of course. Is that all right?
Grand, thank you. I've seen what I need to see.
While you're here, I'll check your blood pressure and pulse quickly. Pop your sleeve up for me.
Certainly. I always get a bit nervous in these rooms, I must say.
Very common. Blood pressure is 142 over 86, and your pulse is 78.
Is that all right, so?
That's grand, thanks. Now, about the warts themselves. Many of them clear up on their own, though it can take months.
Months? I had hoped for something a bit quicker.
I understand. For now, the best thing is not to pick or scratch at them, because that can spread them about.
Right. I'll leave them be, so.
Wash your hands after touching them, and don't share towels with anyone at home.
Towels, yes. I'll tell my husband, he's dreadful for that.
If they catch on your gloves, a plaster over the worst one is perfectly fine.
That's a good idea. I hadn't thought of that.
And waiting it out is a perfectly good plan, you know.
What happens if they don't go away?
Then we'll look again. If they haven't cleared up in three months, come back and see me, and we'll talk about what else can be done.
Three months. That seems fair. And if they start spreading quickly before then?
Then don't wait that long. Ring the surgery and book in sooner.
I will. Thank you ever so much, Doctor.
You're very welcome. Mind how you go on the steps.

clinical_actions.description: Avoid picking or scratching the warts; wash hands after touching them and do not share towels
Cover the worst wart with a plaster if it catches on things

time_reference.value: if they haven't cleared up in three months

clinical_actions.description: Book an earlier appointment if the warts start spreading quickly

follow_up.time_reference: if they haven't cleared up in three months
